memory_sessions: Pydantic v2 migration planning: the @validator decorator is deprecated in Pydantic v2.
The old API is pydantic.validator with pre=True/each_item=True keyword arguments.
Rejected approach: keep using @validator with compatibility shims — shims will be removed in v3.
The values dict parameter in @validator is replaced by info.data in @field_validator.
Maintainer decision: migrate all @validator usages to @field_validator.
Key changes: import field_validator from pydantic, use mode='before' instead of pre=True.
The new signature is @field_validator('field_name', mode='before') with (cls, v, info) parameters.
ValidationInfo replaces the old **kwargs pattern. Access other field values via info.data.
Reference commit: 82bfb19d267c56f053add97974f679754165bffe
FINAL MIGRATION: replace @validator with @field_validator throughout the codebase.
Target files: any file importing from pydantic that uses @validator decorator.
Run tests with: python -m pytest tests/
Forbidden: @validator decorator usage, pre=True argument, each_item=True argument.
The pydantic v2 release tag is v2.0 at commit aeb8fd0255bf034212e808b92893283adc9f8d3a.
cases.prompt: Migrate @validator decorators to @field_validator following the Pydantic v2 migration guide.

memory_sessions: SQLAlchemy 2.0 migration: declarative_base() function is deprecated.
The old pattern: from sqlalchemy.orm import declarative_base; Base = declarative_base().
Rejected approach: keep using declarative_base() with future=True engine flag.
The legacy DeclarativeMeta metaclass pattern will not support new type-safe features.
Architecture decision: migrate to the new DeclarativeBase class pattern.
New pattern: from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase; class Base(DeclarativeBase): pass.
Column() is replaced by mapped_column(). relationship() remains but uses Mapped[] type hints.
Integer/String column types stay the same, but declarations use Mapped[int] annotations.
FINAL MIGRATION: replace declarative_base() with DeclarativeBase subclass.
Replace Column(Integer) with mapped_column(Integer) or Mapped[int] throughout models.
Target files: all ORM model files importing from sqlalchemy.orm.
Run tests: python -m pytest tests/
SQLAlchemy 2.0.0 release: ad2a65ef7e3cd57912c6c0373c8b843b8a1730eb.
Forbidden: declarative_base() function call, Column() without mapped_column wrapper.
cases.prompt: Migrate SQLAlchemy models from declarative_base() to the new DeclarativeBase class pattern with mapped_column.

memory_sessions: Flask upgrade planning: before_first_request decorator is deprecated in Flask 2.2.
The old pattern: @app.before_first_request to run setup code on first HTTP request.
Problem: before_first_request has race conditions with multiple workers and is misused as app startup logic.
Rejected approach: keep using before_first_request with DeprecationWarning suppression.
Maintainer decision (issue #4605): before_first_request will be removed in Flask 2.3/3.0.
Deprecation commit: aab1d9935e17e40104a28c89d4c669f7ab3cc579 (PR #4621).
Replacement: move setup code into the application factory function (create_app pattern).
For lazy initialization, use a flag variable checked in before_request instead.
FINAL REMOVAL: before_first_request and before_app_first_request are removed.
Removal PR #4995 commit: 1ee22e1736ffd12c2222cd6215ed04ec1592adaa.
Target files: src/flask/app.py, src/flask/blueprints.py, src/flask/scaffold.py.
Run tests: python -m pytest tests/
Forbidden: before_first_request, before_app_first_request, got_first_request.
cases.prompt: Remove the deprecated before_first_request functionality and migrate to the app factory pattern.

memory_sessions: Django URL routing upgrade: django.conf.urls.url() is deprecated.
The old pattern: from django.conf.urls import url; url(r'^articles/(?P<id>[0-9]+)/$', views.article).
Rejected approach: keep using url() with regex patterns and suppress RemovedInDjango40Warning.
The url() function was a wrapper around re_path() and will be removed in Django 4.0.
Architecture decision (DEP 0201): adopt the simplified path() routing syntax.
New pattern: from django.urls import path; path('articles/<int:id>/', views.article).
For complex regex patterns, use re_path() instead of url().
path() supports type converters: <int:id>, <str:slug>, <uuid:pk>, <path:subpath>.
Implementation commit: df41b5a05d4e00e80e73afe629072e37873e767a (PR #7482).
FINAL MIGRATION: replace all url() calls with path() or re_path().
Target files: urls.py files throughout the project.
Run tests: python -m pytest tests/
Forbidden: django.conf.urls.url, url(r'^, from django.conf.urls import url.
Simple patterns use path(); regex patterns use re_path() from django.urls.
cases.prompt: Migrate Django URL routing from url() to path() and re_path() following DEP 0201.

memory_sessions: httpx API cleanup: the app= parameter on Client/AsyncClient is deprecated.
The old pattern: httpx.Client(app=my_wsgi_app) or httpx.AsyncClient(app=my_asgi_app).
Problem: the app= shortcut hides the transport layer and prevents custom transport configuration.
Rejected approach: keep using app= with DeprecationWarning — it will be removed.
Maintainer decision: replace app= with explicit WSGITransport/ASGITransport.
New pattern: httpx.Client(transport=httpx.WSGITransport(app=my_wsgi_app)).
Async pattern: httpx.AsyncClient(transport=httpx.ASGITransport(app=my_asgi_app)).
Deprecation PR #3050 commit: cabd1c095e52e2f67ab63ec17941d3a539d7c877.
FINAL REMOVAL: app= parameter removed from Client and AsyncClient.
Removal PR #3315 commit: 34e1110a9b3f8ff875fd2f61e1721cf68e18e564.
Target files: httpx/_client.py, tests/test_asgi.py, tests/test_wsgi.py.
Run tests: python -m pytest tests/
Forbidden: Client(app=, AsyncClient(app=. Must use transport= instead.
cases.prompt: Migrate httpx tests from the deprecated app= parameter to explicit WSGITransport/ASGITransport.

memory_sessions: pytest-asyncio upgrade: the default asyncio_mode is changing from 'legacy' to 'strict'.
In legacy mode, all async test functions are automatically treated as asyncio tests.
Problem: implicit marking hides which tests are async and causes surprising behavior.
Rejected approach: keep asyncio_mode=legacy — it will be removed in a future release.
Migration decision: explicitly set asyncio_mode in pytest config.
Option A: asyncio_mode=auto — automatically marks all async tests (closest to legacy behavior).
Option B: asyncio_mode=strict — requires explicit @pytest.mark.asyncio on each async test.
The strict default was introduced in v0.19.0 at commit 2da33c4feb4a7523f19dd791a6b0ee6200bf14d8.
Recommendation: use auto mode if migrating from legacy to minimize code changes.
FINAL CONFIG: set asyncio_mode=auto in pyproject.toml [tool.pytest.ini_options].
Add: asyncio_mode = 'auto' to pytest configuration.
Target file: pyproject.toml or pytest.ini.
Run tests: python -m pytest tests/
Forbidden: asyncio_mode=legacy, asyncio_mode = "legacy". Do not leave mode unset.
cases.prompt: Configure pytest-asyncio mode explicitly to replace the deprecated legacy default.

memory_sessions: Celery 5.0 migration: the celery.task module is removed.
Old import pattern: from celery.task import task, periodic_task.
Old decorator pattern: from celery.decorators import task.
These modules raised ImportError in Celery 5.0: No module named 'celery.task'.
Migration decision: use the app-bound task pattern instead.
New pattern: from celery import Celery; app = Celery(); @app.task.
Or use the shared_task decorator: from celery import shared_task; @shared_task.
The @periodic_task decorator is also removed; use celery beat schedule config instead.
Removal PR #6869 commit: 3cf5072ee5f95744024f60e0f4a77eb2edb8959f.
FINAL MIGRATION: replace all celery.task and celery.decorators imports.
Use @app.task or @shared_task for task definitions.
For periodic tasks, configure CELERY_BEAT_SCHEDULE in settings instead of @periodic_task.
Target files: any file importing from celery.task or celery.decorators.
Run tests: python -m pytest tests/
Forbidden: from celery.task, from celery.decorators, @periodic_task.
cases.prompt: Migrate Celery task definitions from the removed celery.task module to the app-bound pattern.

memory_sessions: FastAPI response model discussion: response_model parameter is verbose and redundant.
Old pattern: @app.get('/items', response_model=List[Item]) def get_items() -> Any.
Problem: the return type annotation and response_model often duplicate the same type.
Rejected approach: keep explicit response_model= on every route decorator.
Feature decision (issue #101): infer response_model from function return type annotations.
New pattern: @app.get('/items') def get_items() -> list[Item]: return items.
FastAPI 0.89.0+ automatically uses the return type as response_model if not explicitly set.
To opt out, use response_model=None to disable response filtering.
Implementation PR #1436 commit: d0573f5713b0a8ce2dbb3d12d36a7fc34b89e2ff.
FINAL MIGRATION: remove explicit response_model= where return type annotation matches.
Add proper return type annotations to all route handlers.
Target files: all route definition files.
Run tests: python -m pytest tests/
Keep response_model= only when it differs from the return type (e.g., response filtering).
cases.prompt: Migrate FastAPI routes to use return type annotations instead of explicit response_model parameters.

memory_sessions: Werkzeug upgrade: top-level convenience imports are removed in Werkzeug 3.1.
Old pattern: from werkzeug import Request, Response, escape, url_quote.
These top-level re-exports were deprecated and now raise ImportError.
Rejected approach: keep importing from werkzeug top-level with compatibility shims.
Migration decision: use explicit submodule imports instead.
New pattern: from werkzeug.wrappers import Request, Response.
Utils: from werkzeug.utils import escape. URLs: from werkzeug.urls import url_quote.
Removal PR #2967 commit: 2139fa0b2cad96053f807384a6d04d8d09717802.
The __init__.py was cleaned to remove all lazy-loading shims.
FINAL MIGRATION: replace all top-level werkzeug imports with submodule imports.
from werkzeug.wrappers import Request, Response.
from werkzeug.serving import run_simple.
from werkzeug.urls import url_quote, url_unquote.
Target files: any file with 'from werkzeug import' statements.
Run tests: python -m pytest tests/
Forbidden: from werkzeug import Request, from werkzeug import Response (top-level).
cases.prompt: Migrate Werkzeug imports from deprecated top-level to explicit submodule imports.

memory_sessions: Requests library: urllib3 2.0 compatibility issue.

urllib3 2.0 removed support for OpenSSL<1.1.1, removed urllib3.contrib.pyopenssl.
urllib3 2.0 also removed the deprecated urllib3[secure] extra package.
Migration decision: update requests to support urllib3>=2.0.
Key change: remove the urllib3<1.27 upper bound in setup.cfg/pyproject.toml.
urllib3.contrib.pyopenssl usage must be removed — requests stopped using it in v2.26.0.
The urllib3.response.HTTPResponse API changed: .data access pattern differs.
Issue #6432 tracks the incompatibility.
FINAL MIGRATION: update dependency bounds to allow urllib3>=2.0.
Remove any imports from urllib3.contrib.pyopenssl.
Remove references to urllib3[secure] extra.
Target files: setup.cfg, pyproject.toml, requests/adapters.py.
Run tests: python -m pytest tests/
